title: CEM (Circular Estimate Method) – Step-by-step Protocol
author: Marcelo Josende
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xhmfj46
materials: Calibrate the software with help of the reference scale bar of the photo using the tool “Straight” (or similar) of the toolbar. This tool is used to measure the length of the scale bar belong to the photo. A relationship between how many pixels there are in a unit of length (1 mm) has to be made.

steps.title: Prepare nematode suspension tube
steps.instruction: Place the nematode suspension into a Falcon tube sized for its total volume (use a 15 mL tube for ≤15 mL or a 50 mL tube for larger volumes).

steps.title: Prime pipette tip
steps.instruction: Prime the pipette tip by aspirating and dispensing the same liquid/medium (or the nematode suspension) five times to prevent clogging.

steps.title: Transfer aliquot to well
steps.instruction: Gently vortex the Falcon tube, then aspirate 250–500 µL from the middle of the tube and dispense into a well of a 24‑well cell‑culture plate. For nematodes >500 µm, trim the pipette tip tip to avoid clogging.

steps.title: Adjust volume and optional staining
steps.instruction: If the transferred volume is <500 µL, add deionized water to reach exactly 500 µL. Optional: stain the aliquot with 5 % Rose Bengal (300 mg L⁻¹) and incubate 30 min at 80 °C to kill and stretch the worms.

substeps.instruction: Add deionized water to reach 500 µL if needed
Optional: stain with 5 % Rose Bengal (300 mg L⁻¹) and incubate 30 min at 80 °C

steps.title: Homogenize sample in well
steps.instruction: Homogenize the well contents by moving the same pipette tip up and down five times, keeping the tip centered in the well to distribute nematodes evenly.

steps.title: Allow nematodes to settle
steps.instruction: Wait 40–60 seconds for the nematodes to settle to the bottom of the well.

steps.title: Capture microscope images
steps.instruction: Capture images of the well using a light microscope equipped with a camera. Ensure each image includes a scale bar; if a single field does not cover the whole well, acquire overlapping photos for later stitching.

substeps.instruction: If a single field does not cover the well, acquire multiple overlapping photos
Include a scale bar in each image

steps.title: Calibrate image scale (ImageJ)
steps.instruction: In ImageJ/Fiji, open the ‘Analyze’ menu, choose ‘Set Scale’, enter the known distance equal to the scale‑bar length, and set the unit to mm.

substeps.instruction: Enter known distance equal to scale bar

steps.title: Draw 1/10‑well circle
steps.instruction: Select the ‘Oval’ tool, draw a circular shape on the image, and resize it until its diameter matches the calculated 1/10‑well diameter (use the height and width values specific to the plate brand).

substeps.instruction: Resize to calculated 1/10‑well diameter (height and width)

steps.title: Fix and replicate circles
steps.instruction: Drag the circle to the well wall, press Ctrl + B to fix it, then repeat the placement and fixing three more times to obtain four circles.

substeps.instruction: Repeat three more times for total of four circles

steps.title: Count nematodes within circles
steps.instruction: Zoom the image, activate the ‘Multi‑point’ tool, and click each nematode that lies completely inside a circle to record counts (exclude animals crossing the circle boundary).

substeps.instruction: Click each fully‑inside nematode to count

steps.title: Extrapolate counts to whole well
steps.instruction: Calculate the average count from the four circles and extrapolate this value to estimate the total number of nematodes in the entire well (or in the original suspension volume).

substeps.instruction: Compute average of four circle counts
Extrapolate to whole well or suspension volume
